question: How many Swiss regions will be classified as "Extremely Dry" according to the Swiss drought platform on December 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: In October 2026 official sources described extreme drought across the whole Midland, with the Jura and Basel severely affected. The 29 Oct bulletin says recent rain gave temporary regional relief, and most regions outside the central/eastern Alps show only mild-moderate 30-day shortfalls. A dry early November, then near-normal rain, is forecast; the bulletin expects deficits to persist. The platform map counts could not be read directly. A month of near-normal rain with low winter evaporation often drops regions out of the top category, but lakes and groundwater lag. So substantial mass is on 0-1 regions (below the lower bound), with a right-skewed tail if dryness persists. No human market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers: none).
calls.dossier:
- Platform trockenheit.admin.ch: situation map dated until 2026-11-01 (updated 11-02); 5 categories from 'not dry' to 'extremely dry'; per-region counts not extractable from page text (interactive map/list).
- Drought bulletin 2026-10-29: drought persists; recent precip gave temporary regional relief; overall situation tense. Most affected: central/eastern Alps (Uri, Glarus Alps, Surselva, N. Graubünden) with 30-day precip deficits of 50-70%; other regions mild-moderate 30-day deficits, moderate-severe 90-day deficits; parts of W/NW Switzerland positive 30-day balance. Next bulletin 2026-11-05.
- Outlook (bulletin 10-29): early Nov high pressure and dry, then westerly flow with near-normal precip on northern Alps; deficits expected to persist.
- BAFU/admin.ch Oct 2026: whole Midland Yverdon to St. Gallen Rhine Valley described as extreme drought; Jura and Basel severely affected; Bodensee, Walensee, Zürichsee and smaller lakes at extremely low levels for the season in mid-Oct.
- Swissinfo (autumn 2026): 30-day rainfall <50% of normal, some areas 15-35%; river flows at 10-30-yr return-period lows in Jura/Plateau.
- Context: August 2026 driest since 1864; since April only 61% of normal rain.
- Status quo: drought ongoing, with relief starting in some regions; the category mix on Dec 1 depends on November rain.
- Resolves off the trockenheit.admin.ch region classification accessed on/after 2026-12-01, not off news descriptions.
- Event window: single snapshot on 2026-12-01; as of 2026-11-04, about 27 days remain.
- Searched but not found: the current count of extremely dry regions, the total number of regions, historical counts from 2018/2022, and any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: Late-autumn Swiss drought episodes (e.g., 2018, 2022) a month after first autumn rains: number of regions still in the top drought category

calls.reasoning: As of ~Nov 1-3 2026, news and the Oct 29 bulletin report a handful of regions with extreme drought (Lake Zurich area, Glarus Alps, Rhine valley; bulletin flags Uri, Glarus, Surselva, N. Graubünden), with most of the plateau/Alps dry-very dry and Ticino recovered. CDI = second-highest of 30d/90d/730d precip, soil moisture and discharge classes, so slow-changing discharge and 90-day deficits keep the index sticky. First 10 days of November forecast nearly dry, second half wetter (moderate). Status quo ~3-6 extreme regions; a wet late November could push it to 0-1 (priced as 25% below range), continued dryness could expand it. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers: none). Couldn't read per-region map data directly, so evidence is thin and the distribution is kept wide.
calls.dossier:
- Resolution: resolves off the CDI map at trockenheit.admin.ch (number of regions in class 'Extremely dry', class 5 of 5) when Metaculus checks on/after 2026-12-01. It does NOT resolve off the canton warning levels (Gefahrenstufen 1-5) shown on the natural-hazards portal or the swisstopo briefing; those are a different measure.
- Event window: a single snapshot on 2026-12-01; as of 2026-11-04 about 0% of any window has elapsed; ~27 days until the snapshot.
- CDI method (trockenheit.admin.ch/en/drought/drought-index): classes for 30d precip, 90d precip, 730d precip, modelled soil moisture and discharge/water level; final CDI = SECOND-highest class (drops the highest outlier). Values 1 (not dry) to 5 (extremely dry).
- The platform map shows 'Situation until 11/01/2026', updated 11/02/2026; text: recent precipitation temporarily eased drought regionally, overall situation remains tense.
- Bulletin 2026-10-29 (next 11-05): most extreme stress in the central/eastern Alps (Uri, Glarus, Surselva, North Graubünden), 90-day deficits of 50-70%; W/NW Switzerland 30-day balance locally improved; rivers and large lakes still exceptionally low; groundwater low; soil moisture deficit large to extreme on the Alpine north side and plateau. Forecast: high pressure in early Nov, deficits expected to persist or grow.
- Bote/Tages-Anzeiger 2026-11-02: extreme drought around Lake Zurich, Glarus Alps, Rhine Valley; large parts of plateau/Alps dry-very dry; only Ticino recovered. First 10 days of Nov: hardly any precipitation (fog, drizzle at most); outlooks suggest more rain days with light-moderate amounts in the second half of November. A strong El Niño could mean a mild/wet winter, but the polar vortex is weakening early (colder signal); seasonal outlook uncertain.
- Context: Apr-Sep 2026 was the driest summer half-year since 1864 (56% of normal precipitation); Lake Zurich, Lake Constance and Lago Maggiore are at record lows for the season.
- Watson 2026-09-21: large areas of the north side were 'dry' to 'very dry' on the map at that time; the south side was more relaxed.
- Searched for but not found: the total number of CDI regions on the map; the exact current count of class-5 regions (the map is interactive and not in the page text; the opendata.swiss dataset returned 403); a history of counts in past droughts.
- Warning-level data (a different measure): swisstopo briefing 2026-11-03 shows 20 cantons at level 4, 5 at level 2 and Ticino at level 1.
- Markets: none found.
calls.reference_class: Swiss CDI regional classification persistence over ~4-week horizons during prolonged multi-season droughts (2018, 2022, 2025-26 analogues), anchored on current count of extreme regions

calls.reasoning: geo.admin identify on ch.bafu.trockenheitsindex (week 26.10-01.11.2026) shows 0 of 38 regions extremely dry, 19 very dry, 7 dry, 11 slightly dry, 1 not dry. A search summary of a BAFU report says about 20 of 38 were extremely dry in September (original not opened), so late-October rain cut the count sharply. River flow and lake levels are still low and the platform says the situation remains tense, so a dry or blocked November could push very-dry regions back to extreme; a normal or wet November keeps the count at 0-1 (below the 1.5 range minimum). No human market found (Polymarket and Manifold per harness search; my own searches found none; Kalshi and bookmakers not checked).
sources: WebSearch summary: September 2026 BAFU count of 20/38 regions extremely dry
WebSearch summary: November 2026 Switzerland precipitation outlook (wetterprognose-wettervorhersage.de, meteo-ch.ch)
calls.dossier:
- geo.admin identify, layer ch.bafu.trockenheitsindex, valid 26.10.2026-01.11.2026, queried 2026-11-04: 38 regions in total. Extremely dry: 0. Very dry: 19 (Bernese Plateau, Oberaargau, Upper Emmental, Freiamt, W and E Central Switzerland, E Bernese Oberland, E Swiss Plateau, Lake Zurich Region, Uri Alps, Surselva, Glarus Alps, N-Central and S-Central Grisons, Rhine Valley, Prättigau, Visp valleys, Goms). Dry: 7. Slightly dry: 11 (Jura, Western Plateau, Lake Geneva, Chablais, N Valais, Ticino, Upper Engadine). Not dry: 1 (Sottoceneri). Confirmed by two separate queries.
- A search-engine summary attributed to BAFU says that in September 2026 20 of 38 regions were extremely dry, 13 very dry, 2 dry and 3 slightly dry. Original not opened; unverified.
- Another search summary claimed 5 regions extremely dry as of 1 Nov. It conflicts with the API data and is probably a summarizer error.
- trockenheit.admin.ch bulletin, updated 02.11.2026 (situation to 01.11): drought persists; recent rain temporarily eased it in some regions; overall situation remains tense.
- Warning map (ch.bafu.trockenheitswarnkarte), from a separate query: 25 regions at level 4 'high danger' since late June; Jura, W Plateau, Lake Geneva and Engadine cut to level 2 on 22 Oct; Ticino and Grisons southern valleys cut to level 1 on 29 Oct.
- Swissinfo, 12 Oct 2026: rain brought only temporary relief; 30-day rainfall 15-50% of normal in many areas; river flows at 10-30-year lows; record low on the Upper Rhine.
- Swissinfo, 21 Aug 2026: hottest summer on record; driest August since 1864; Lake Constance and Lake Zurich at record lows.
- CDI method (geo.admin): index 1-5 relative to the season, combining precipitation, modeled soil moisture and river flow or lake level; updated weekly. Slow-moving parts (river flow, lakes) are still in deficit.
- Secondary weather outlooks: blocking high with dry weather to about 9 Nov; precipitation signal around 10 Nov, stronger in the south; drying again from about 13 Nov. Monthly climatology sites suggest near-normal November totals.
- Status quo: 0 extremely dry, with 19 regions one class below.
- Resolves off the platform's displayed drought-index map/classes (the 5-class CDI) when accessed on or after 1 Dec 2026, probably the week ending about 29-30 Nov. NOT off the separate warning map (danger levels).
- Event window: the snapshot at access on or after 2026-12-01; as of 2026-11-04, about 4 weekly updates remain.
- Searched but not found: weekly time series of extremely-dry counts (the CSV zip on data.geo.admin.ch could not be downloaded); MeteoSwiss official monthly outlook; any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: Week-to-week persistence of the CDI extremely-dry class count in the platform's 38 regions during the 2026 drought; status quo (current count) carried 4 weekly updates forward

calls.reasoning: Platform API (ch.bafu.trockenheitsindex, week 26.10-01.11.2026): 0 of 38 regions extremely dry, 19 very dry. Status quo is 0. A dry first third of November, then forecast near-normal rain, makes 0-1 the most likely result. The index is the second-highest of five measures, and river flow and lakes remain in deficit, so a blocked dry November could push several very-dry regions back to class 5. 50% is placed below the 1.5 lower bound, the 0.5 maximum allowed (my earlier answer used 0.55 and was rejected). The in-range distribution is right-skewed. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: Runs 1-2 inferred several extremely dry regions from news reports. Run 3 queried the official index layer directly and found 0 of 38, confirmed twice. I trust the API, since the news 'extreme drought' wording likely refers to the separate danger-level warning map. Whether November turns dry or wet is a judgment call; the forecasts favour near-normal rain after about 10 Nov. Status quo of 0 plus slow re-escalation puts heavy mass below 1.5. The 0.5 cap is applied.

disagreements.verdict: Run 3's direct API query (0 of 38) outweighs inference from news wording; news likely refers to the separate warning map

disagreements.claim: November rainfall will be enough to keep the count at 0-1
disagreements.verdict: Forecasts point to near-normal rain after a dry start; I lean toward the low side, capped at 0.5

disagreements.verdict: Unverified search summary; used only to judge how large swings can be
